ELECTION OF CEIIIRMA.N AND VICE-CHAIRMAN. The fortnightly meeting of this Board, which was also the annuli meeting, was held at Dattoa Woratiouee. on Tuesday, when there were present—Messrs J Mosley- Williams (chairman), J Stokes (vice-chairman), A R Nerinan, T Reynolds, J Meadowcroft, the Rural District Couneillore, with Mr G F Ashton (deputy clerk). RHELECTION OF CHAIRMAN. Mr. Baxter proposed that Mr. J. Mesley-Williams be chairman of the Board for the ensuing year. Ha was sure he had filled the position well durine the past year, and he did not think they ought to make changes unless they were really necessary. (Hear, heir.) Mr. Spruce seconded. He thought the very admirable manner in which Mr. Williams had discharged the duties of the office during the past year was entitled to seine consideration. The propositioa was carried unanimously. Mr. Weliams theceupen task the chair. Hs was much obliged to the members for re-appointing him to that office, and for the manner in which they had supperted him during the past year. He hoped .they might get along as comfortably and as happily as they had done in the past. He suggested that in future the meetings of the Board should commence at 12.30 instead of 12.45. That Was a matter which they might consider later on. Mr; Knowles moved the re-appointment of Mr. J. ' Stokes as vice-chairman. Mr. Woodward seconded, and the motion was carried unanimously. Mr. Stokes briefly returned thanks. THE COMMITTEES. The several committees of the B oard were re-appoia- ted with but slight alterations. On the motion of Mr. A. R. Norman seconded by Mr. T Reynolds, Mrs. Baker, of Ruucora, was added to the Ladies Visiting Com- mittee.— The Chairman and Vice-Chairman were appointed as follows ;—Finance Committee, Mr. S. i Woodward, chairman, and Mr. T. Wright, vice-chair- man; Relief Supervision Committee, Mr. T. Lea. chair- ' man, and Mr. J. Ideadowcroft, vica-chtircaan ; Visiting Committee, Mr. A. R. Norman, chairman, and Mr. Admiral Jones-Parry, vice-chairman. NEWTOWN VACANCY. Messrs. T. Lee,and Thomas Reynolds gave notice that a vacancy had occurred in the offi to of guardian of the poor for the Newtown Ward of the Parish of Runcorn by the death of Mr. S. Yarwood and requested th it pro- ceedings should be taken to fill the vacancy. Tbe Clerk intimated that notices would be duly published for the election of a guardian for the ward. THE LADIES AND THE DOCTOR—"NOTHING LIKE MILK." The Rock, Frodsnam, April 22ad.—Dear Sir—i sin obliged for yours ot the 12:h tilt eiclmeing extract copy from the Ladies Visiting Book. Our dietaries have been ' revised recently and sanctioned by the Local Govern- ment Board, and compare vary faveurebly with similar institutions. The guardians place no restrictions as to the quantity of any extras and milk and beef tea are freely , and liberally allowed, vide milk account vide medical relief b mk. There is no better nourishment than mak and I cry with the dairymaid" Milk, more milk ; milk for evermore, for there. s nothing like milk." I consider the aged and young chtiare.n well cared far. I regret to remind the ladies Oa, it is not one of the traditions 'of the medical profession to treat by " meagre diet which perpetuates and cannot relieve," and tnat the treatment in this Workhouse is no exception.—Yours truly T. J. SELBY, M. 8., L.R.C.P., med;cel officer. The matter WaS deferred to the Master. FINANCE COMMITTEE. Outralief was gramed as follows : Runcorn £BO ; Fredsham £24; and Budworth £22. The total payments for the day amounted to £215 12s 61, alter which a eal- ance of £660 3: 61 was lett in tee treasurer's The finance report was adppted on the motion of Me. S. Woodward, seconded by Mr. T. Wright. THE PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEE. THE RATING OF GROUND VALUES. Mr. Mclntyre said the Parliamentary Committee had had under consideration a numbir of questions sub- mitted by other Uoious. The first was a resolution from the Launces'on Uuion with reference to the law with re- gard to women wiao entered the workhouse for the pur- pose of being confined. The Leuncescon Board desired that power should be given to the Board of Guardians to detain in the worknouse for such period as the Medical Officer might think necessary (not ex- ceeding twelve months) any mother of an illegitimate child born in the workhouse. There were not many of these cases dealt with at the Rueeoro Workhouse and the Committee recommended that no action should he taken. The next matter the Committee dealt with was a cemmunication from the Hackney Union who desired to give the conscientious objector to vaccination more liberty that the present law allowed. The Committee were not prepared to go any further in that dee ccion at any rate,and they deceied that no action stiaild be taken. 'rue Kings Norton Uaion also submitted a commuaicatna wite reference to vaccination, and the committee re- commended no action in that case. Toe Kettering Union , forwarded a report emoodying certain suggestions with ' reference to old age pensions. The Parliamentary Com- mittee considered that the time was not ripe yet for the , Ruucorn Union to give any definite decision on this question, and they recommended that its consideration sheuld be deferred. The Todnaorden Union asked their adoption of the following resolution with respect to the Inebriates Act :—"That having regard to the provisiene of the above act for the detention in Ine- briate Reformatories of habitual drunkards. and lurther, as floe general regulations for the manage- ment of sucu reformatories are framed for the purp isC of reclaiming inmates it is desirable that the exieting facilities for the sale of intoxicating liquors be placed under greater restriction." Trio committee rec ommended that the letter lie on the table, as they theu;ht it was scarcely within the scope of their work at the present time. It was more a question for the justices to deal with. The next matter considered was a letter from the Land Laws Reform Association with reference to the rating of ground values. (Hear, hear, from Mr. Roy- lance.) That was an important question that had been agitated and was likely to be the cause of agitation be- fore any legislation could taken place. rue committee recommended that no action be taken. Mr. Reylauce : A portion of them. Mr. Livaker : A big majority of them. Mr. Mclntyre: Yes. I must say there was a large majority. Mr. Mclntyre moved that the report of the Committee be adopted. Mr. Linaker seconded. Mr. Roylance thought the resolution from the Land Laws Reform Association deserved the attention of the Council. He could not for the life of him see why these ground rents should be exempt from rating. Supposing he (Mr. Roylance) took a farm say from Mr. Linaker, and part of his land adjoined the highway. Admiral Jones-Parry or some other gentleman drove past and said "That will make a nice spot for a hcuse." He chose a piece of land nearest the highway and Mr. Linaker said " You shall have it if you will pay about four times the amount Roylance does." He bought the land and he paid no rates upon it. Mr. Linaker: He does pay tates upon that cep. tainly. Mr. Roylance contended that ground rents were not taxed at all,and he thought they ought to be taxed. Mr. Linaker: You are wrong. Mr. Roylance: Why does the association put this be- fore us? Admiral Jones-Parry drew attention to the fact that it was 2.30. He really nelieved this was not a question for the Board of Guardians. It would take a whole month, and, therefore, it was simply wastiug their time.

Mr. Woodward said there were difficulties no doubt with referetic3 to the taxation of the ground values, but the committee felt they were not in a position to deal with the question fairly and squarely all round, and he objected to dealing with it piece meal by recommenda- tions which he dui not understand. Mr. Pilling : It was not ordered to lie on th 3 table. The matter was deferred. Mr. Roylance's amendment was notseconded, and the report of the ,:onomittee was adopted. THE SHEDDING ACCOMMODATION. The Board proceed:id to consider tenders for the erec• tioa of shedding at the workhous3 to accommodate members's conveyances and for the purpose of stone breaking. Five tenders were sent in, and that of Me. Frederick Walinsley, of Whitley, amounting to £9O, was accepted.

div.head: LICENSENG PROSECIMON AT
div.p: LICENSENG PROSECIMON AT
F RODSHAM.
A LANDLORD_AND TEIE THREE MILE mum

At Frodsharn Petty Sessions on Wednesday. before Me*srs. C. Reynolds (in the chair). J. Ockleston,and G. C. Taylor, David Wilkin Brown, licaosee of the Bridge Hotel, Prodshatri, was summoned at the instance of the police for keeping his house open during prohibited hours for the sale of intoxicating liver, cu Sunday. the 19th of March !alt.—There was also a charge pre- ferred against faur young men : Charles Dodd, Thomas Pollard, James Booth, and John Howard, of being found on licensed premises during prohibited h3urs at Prod- sham at 11.40 a.m. on tne 19th of March.—Mr. Chester, appeared for the police, and Mr. A. Browne, splicitor, Warrington, for the landlord of the public- houfe.—The charge against the licensee was first pro- ceeded with.

Police Constable Gregory, stated that on Sunday tho 1911 of March last, he in company with Police Constable Wylie went along the railway for the purpose of keeping a watch upon the Bridge Inn, and also upon the Aston Arms, Frodsham. At about 10.20 they sag, a number of men go into the Bridge inn. Subsequently at about 11.40 a.m., he went into the Bridge Inn, in company with Policy Sergeant Bsurne. They went inby the front door which was unfastined. In the lobby he met two men viz., Thomas Wilson and Thomas Robinson. He also saw the barman John Thomas Booth. The proprie• tor was not present whln they went in. On going to the smoke-room he found about 13 men there all with pint cup 3 containing beer before them ; that was, there was beer in most of them. In the front parlour there were two men. When the landlord came downstairs he

heard Sergeant Bourne ask him about the men. Sergeant Bourne said "Some of the men came from Halton, r]ui some from Runcorn, and that there were men present who had not 001113 the 3 mile limit." Sergeant Bourne took their names in his presence. Thomas Pollard, tanner, Halton ; Charles Dedd, Old flail, Halton, tanner ; James Booth, and John lloward, both gave their address as 26, Halton-road, Runcorn, saying put us both down for the same address. He knew now that they resided at Westoa.—Cross-examined by Mr. Browns: The four men, Pollard, Dodd. Booth,and Howard were the only men who had come from within the 3 mile limit that he knew of. Booth and Howard had given them the wrong address, saying" 26, Halton- road," whilst they lived elsewhere. He could net say whether they had also given a wrong address to the barman. Mr. Browne : Ai a matter of fact the men told the barmen they resided in 15, Duke-street, Runcorn.—Witness knew nothing about that.—Qiestioned as to whether the man Booth had shown him a half-crown, and told him be bad come to Frodsham to pay for a child of his ? Gregory replied that the man showed him half-a-crown, but he did not catch what he said about it. Sergeant A. J. Bourne corroborated the evidence of P.C. Gree,ory. Themes Pollard and Charles Doid gave tneir addresses to him. The wiadow of the smoke-room looked out into the road, but he noticed that the blind was down, On going into the rooms he took the names of those present. When the landlord came downstairs he t)ld him that some of the men Calll9 from Halton which was within the 3 miles limit, and asked hires about it. The landlord replied that" he had been informed he he was doing right in serving these men from Runcora," and added "if he was doing wrong he was doing it innocently." There was I beer and porter before the men Pollard and Didd.—By Mr. Browne: Witness saw Booth produce half-a-crown and say something about his child. If Booth and Howard had come from Hilton-road.Runcorn near Fli4tifield tannery they would have been without the limit.
Constable A. Price, Frodsham, gave evidence as to watching the house and seeing a number of men going in.

Sergeant Edwin Clays, said h, measured the distance from tee Bridge Inn to the houses of the persons found on the premises : Thomas Pollard. resided at Main. r.reet, Halton, distance 2 miles, 1204 yards ; Charles DocH, ad Hall, Runcorn. 2 miles, 1557 yards ; James Booth, We..tan, 2 miles, 603 yards; acid Jolla How trd the same.He had measured with a chain 66ft., in length, an 1 80 inks to to the mile.—ln answer to the Chairman this witness said there was a stone—presumably a mile stone—at the corner of the street in Halton which bore upon it" 3i miles to Frodshatn. Charles Ilumphreys gave evidence of the police re- ceiving the addresses from the men as stat?d. Mr. Browne, for the defence, contended that his client had served the men believing them to be bona fide travel- lers. He would only call the barman Jolla Thomas Booth, who would state that he had asked all the men as they came in "Where they c sine from?" and " Whether they were ping further ?" which was all that he could do. Perhaps the Bench had not heard the address of the learned judge at the Quarter Sessions the other thy when a publican was indicted for refusing to serv3 cyclists. But what he said was that it had taken them five hours to decide what a publican had to do in a moment. He (Mr. Browne) thought that the publican was practically " b.,tween the devil and the deep blue sea," for if he did not serve the men he was liable to b 3 indicted at Quarter Sessions, and if he did serve he was prosecuted on another count.

Jo-tin Thomas Booth, barman, at the Bridge Inn,stated he had been there for five years, and his master only two years. Mr. Browne had asked Constable Price whether he was right in serving people from Runcorn, and be htd replied in the affirmative. He asked all the men where they came from, and whether they were going on, and upon receiving satisfactory replits he served them with drink. Booth was tho only RIAU out of the four proceeded against that he knew.— Booth and Howard came to the door together and said they came from 15, Duke-street, Runcorn. The other two men said Halton-road near the Highfield Tannery. He n. ver served anyone who cime from Halton.—Cross- examiued by Mr. Giles: He also said he asked the police where they came from? but they went past him without answering. _ _

The magistrates dismissed the case, observing that they evnsidered that no case had been made out against the landlord.—Thornas Pollird, Charles Didd, James 13Joth, and John Howard then pleaded guilty to being on the premises during prohiNted hours.—Tney at ited that they had not given wrong addre3ses, and were under the impression that they ha i come the requisite distance.—They were each fuid 5 and 8. 61. costs.

Some of our alarmists are continually threatening us with "bolts from the blue" and this week con- siderable capital has been made out of a report that the United Alkali iirrks Co., contemplate an exten- sion of their soap industry. TiliB has been magni • fled somewhat by a correspondent to a contempor- ary who infers that the Company contemplate re- moving the present soap works from Runcorn. I am informed on reliable authority that such is not the intention of the company. I would also console my readers by quoting Mr. F. J. Norman, J.P., (one of the Company's managers)who in a speech on the "town and trade of Runcorn" referred to the matter "as an alarmist's report entirely without foundation.' A lot of comfort can be gathered from that statement.

At the meeting of the Runcorn Rural District Council and the Board of Guardians the relAring chairmen Messrs. Joseph Knowles, and J. Mosley Williams were re-elected chairmen, and Ale:srs. S. Woodward and J. Stokes vice-chairmen respec- tively. The four are gentlemen well versed in the work they have in hand, and well qualified to occupy their positions.

The directors of the Runcorn Gas Company an- nounce a discount of 2,1 per 1,000 cubic feet for the quarter ending June 30th, on all accounts paid within a month of that date, whici is a feature of great interest to all consumers of gas. Doubtless this conditional reduction will be the forerunner of a permanent reduction in the price of this house- hold commodity, and if availed of, will effect a great saving to all.

At length the Library Committee are taking steps towards the provision of a catalogue; and at tile meeting ol that body on Tuesday night went so far as to instruct the Librarian to secure estimates for an edition of 1,000 copies. Some desultiry discus- sion took place concerning the" worrying" the magazines receive at the hands of numerou3 readers who turn over the pages with unnecessary rough- ness. As this refers particularly to our young readers, I hope they will take it to heart and exet- cise a little more care.

Wherever do the bad smells come from? is often the query of those people living in the vicinity of the lligh-street end of Devonshire-square. The answer invariably is "Goodness knows !" But the bad smells are there, and it is my opinion they are caused by defective drainage or something of the kind. Some people hint at the obnoxious effluvia emanating from premises in that locality wich which it is not their desire to interfere, lan a little more charitable, but would like to be rid of the smell all the same.

The Rural District Council of Runcorn is a body which carries out its business with a despatch equalled by few such bodies, but I venture to sug- gest that it would—in the long run—be saving con- siderable time, and the patience of the membars if it decided that the standing orders of the Parlia- mentary Committee should be: "Everything sub- mitted to us shall for ever lie on the table." I only make the suggestion because 99 per cent. of the de- cisions of the committee work out to that, aud it would be but small loss were the remaining one per cent. sacrificed.

Runcorn Liberal Club has arranged to run an ex- cursion to Windermere on or about Whit-Tuesday lam given to uatleNtand, and the out is being eagerly,talked about. Given a fine day it is doubt ful whether a more enjoyable trip could bs uoutens- lated, and I wish the duo wall in its undertaking.-

div.head: APPLETON PARISH COUNCIL MEETING.
div.p: APPLETON PARISH COUNCIL MEETING.

The Parish Council meeting took place in the Appleton Thorn Schoolroom the other avening,when there were present—Messrs J Marsh, J Whitlow, H Darbyshire, J Britch, E Britch, R Rnighsedge, anti J Ellison (clerk). After the members had duly signed the declaration ot acceptance of office, the following gentlemen were ap- pointed for the ensuing year: —Mr J Marsh, chairman i • Mr II Eyes, vice-chairman; Messrs R Tickle and T Ditchfield, overseers. The members of the Council, including Mr J Knowles, district councillor; and Mr Bradford, district coun- cillor for Grappenhall, were afterwards invited to dinner at the Thorn Inn by the Chairman, Mr J Marsh. An excellent spread was . provided by the Host, Mr J Britch. The remainder of the evening was spent in a very enjoyable manner.
